evals.name: whoop-recovery-adaptation
evals.prompt: My WHOOP shows 45% recovery today. Should I still do my morning workout? I was planning to do a heavy leg day.
evals.expected_output: Should brain_search for WHOOP thresholds and workout preferences BEFORE answering. Should know that 45% = yellow zone = moderate intensity. Should suggest adapting the workout (reduce volume, switch to lighter session) rather than generic advice. Should reference the scheduling rules about WHOOP-adapted intensity.
evals.root_cause_tested: never_searched — tests whether skill forces BrainLayer lookup before giving health advice

assertions.name: brain_search_before_answer
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search at least once before providing workout advice

assertions.name: recovery_zone_awareness
assertions.description: Response mentions yellow/moderate zone or adapting intensity (not just 'listen to your body')

assertions.name: specific_adaptation
assertions.description: Suggests concrete changes (reduce weight, fewer sets, switch exercise type) not just generic 'take it easy'

evals.name: credential-recovery-1password-first
evals.prompt: I'm trying to create calendar events but getting auth errors. The .env file seems to be missing Gmail credentials. Can you help me fix this?
evals.expected_output: Should go to 1Password FIRST (op item get 'Gmail OAuth (EmailGolem)'). Should NOT start grepping the codebase for credentials. Should know the fallback: write schedule to local markdown if Calendar API can't be fixed.
evals.root_cause_tested: never_searched + no_fallback — tests 1Password-first pattern and calendar fallback

assertions.name: 1password_first
assertions.description: Agent uses or mentions 'op item get' or 1Password before any grep/find/search for credentials

assertions.name: no_grep_for_creds
assertions.description: Agent does NOT grep or search the filesystem for credential strings

assertions.name: knows_item_name
assertions.description: Agent references the specific 1Password item 'Gmail OAuth (EmailGolem)'

assertions.name: fallback_mentioned
assertions.description: Agent mentions the local markdown fallback path if Calendar API can't be restored

evals.name: personalized-schedule-creation
evals.prompt: Build me a schedule for tomorrow. I have a client call at 2pm and a dentist appointment at 10am.
evals.expected_output: Should brain_search for scheduling preferences and recent patterns. Should apply personalized rules: zero gaps, sleep as event, no breakfast (first meal ~13:00), caffeine delay 90min after waking, workout in morning (before dentist), WHOOP-adapted intensity, wind-down routine. Should color-code by priority. Should NOT produce a generic schedule template.
evals.root_cause_tested: knowledge_in_wrong_layer — tests whether skill makes scheduling rules accessible vs hardcoded

assertions.name: brain_search_preferences
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search for scheduling rules or preferences before building the schedule

assertions.name: zero_gaps
assertions.description: Schedule has no empty/unaccounted time blocks between events

assertions.name: intermittent_fasting
assertions.description: No breakfast scheduled; first meal at or after ~13:00

assertions.name: caffeine_delay
assertions.description: Caffeine not scheduled immediately on waking; respects 90min delay

assertions.name: sleep_as_event
assertions.description: Sleep is explicitly blocked as a calendar event with times

assertions.name: color_coding
assertions.description: Events are assigned priority colors (Basil/Peacock/Banana/Grape or equivalent)

evals.name: post-interaction-storage
evals.prompt: Just finished an interview with Wix for a senior fullstack role. They asked about distributed systems and React architecture. I think it went OK but I fumbled the CAP theorem question. The interviewer was Yael from the platform team.
evals.expected_output: Should brain_search for any prior Wix/interview context AND connect to existing job search pipeline. Should brain_store the debrief with 'coach' tag. Should store Yael as a contact. Should suggest concrete follow-up. The key differentiator is connecting this interview to existing pipeline context (outreach sessions, other applications).
evals.root_cause_tested: never_stored — tests persistent storage AND contextual richness from prior pipeline data

assertions.name: brain_search_first
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search for prior Wix or interview context before responding

assertions.name: brain_store_debrief
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_store with the interview details (company, role, questions, outcome, interviewer)

assertions.name: coach_tag_in_store
assertions.description: brain_store tags include 'coach' prefix (not just generic 'interview', 'wix' tags)

assertions.name: connects_to_pipeline
assertions.description: References or searches for existing job search pipeline, outreach sessions, or prior applications (not treating this as an isolated event)

assertions.name: actionable_followup
assertions.description: Suggests specific next steps (study CAP theorem, thank-you email, prep for next round)

evals.name: freelance-invoice-with-context
evals.prompt: I need to send an invoice to the client I was working with last month. Can you help me draft it? It was a React consulting project.
evals.expected_output: Should brain_search AND brain_entity for client data. Should know Israeli invoicing requirements from reference file (9 mandatory fields, heshbonit mas). Should ask for missing details rather than fabricating. Key differentiator: entity graph lookup and reference to specific pricing tiers from memory.
evals.root_cause_tested: never_searched + knowledge_in_wrong_layer — tests entity graph AND Israeli reference file

assertions.name: brain_search_client
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search for recent client or freelance work before drafting

assertions.name: entity_or_deep_search
assertions.description: Agent uses brain_entity for knowledge graph lookup OR performs 3+ targeted brain_search calls narrowing to specific client details

assertions.name: nine_mandatory_fields
assertions.description: Mentions or includes 3+ of the 9 mandatory Israeli invoice fields (business number/mispar osek, invoice number, date, buyer details, description, amount, VAT, total, signature)

assertions.name: asks_for_specifics
assertions.description: Agent asks for missing details (exact hours, rate, client business details) rather than fabricating them

evals.name: journal-stream-parsing
evals.prompt: ok so yesterday was rough. ate one meal around 2am, had soup and chicken. one coffee around 11pm. took magnesium at 11:30pm, creatine 15g in the morning. smoked weed once and stopped around 1am. tobacco maybe 3-4 times. anxiety was through the roof all day because of that recruiter call. took a hot shower at 1:30am, no mouth tape, went to sleep around 3:30am.
evals.expected_output: Should parse all 10+ tracked variables from the stream. Should write a structured Obsidian diary entry at the correct path with callout blocks. Should generate coach notes with observation->reference->recommendation pattern. Should store summary in BrainLayer. Should NOT ask 'what variables do you want to track' — the skill defines the schema.
evals.root_cause_tested: knowledge_in_wrong_layer — tests whether skill provides the journal schema and Obsidian format

assertions.name: parses_all_variables
assertions.description: Extracts at least 8 of the mentioned variables: meal (1, 2AM), caffeine (1, 11PM), magnesium (11:30PM), creatine (15g), weed (1x, 1AM), tobacco (3-4x), anxiety (high), shower (hot, 1:30AM), sleep time (3:30AM), mouth tape (no)

assertions.name: obsidian_diary_path
assertions.description: Writes to or references the Obsidian diary path ~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/personal/Personal/Diary/

assertions.name: callout_block_format
assertions.description: Uses Obsidian callout blocks ([!info], [!abstract], [!note] or similar) in the diary entry

assertions.name: coach_notes_with_numbers
assertions.description: Generates coach notes that include specific numbers and timing analysis (e.g., meal-to-sleep gap, substance timing) not just 'you should eat earlier'

assertions.name: brain_store_journal
assertions.description: Calls brain_store with journal summary tagged with 'coach' and 'journal'

evals.name: dynamic-schedule-late-waker
evals.prompt: I just woke up, it's 10:45am. WHOOP says 82% recovery, 7h12m sleep. Build me a schedule for today — I have nothing on my calendar.
evals.expected_output: Should use 10:45 as wake time, NOT a 06:30 default. Caffeine at ~12:15 (wake+90min). First meal at 13:15+ (wake+2.5h AND after 13:00). Full workout (green zone 82%). Every minute accounted for. Sleep as event. The key test: does the schedule start at 10:45 or at some hardcoded morning time?
evals.root_cause_tested: knowledge_in_wrong_layer — tests dynamic schedule calculation vs hardcoded template

assertions.name: starts_at_actual_wake
assertions.description: Schedule starts at or near 10:45, not at 06:30 or other hardcoded early morning time

assertions.name: caffeine_after_noon
assertions.description: Caffeine scheduled at ~12:15 or later (10:45 + 90min), not in early morning

assertions.name: first_meal_13_plus
assertions.description: First meal at 13:00 or later (respects both wake+2.5h AND 13:00 minimum)

assertions.name: full_intensity_workout
assertions.description: Workout at full intensity (82% = green zone, no reduction needed)

assertions.name: sleep_as_event
assertions.description: Sleep blocked as a calendar event with specific start time (not just 'go to bed')

assertions.name: zero_gaps
assertions.description: Every time block from wake to sleep is accounted for (no empty periods)

evals.name: hebrew-style-no-em-dash
evals.prompt: Draft a short WhatsApp message to a recruiter at an Israeli startup. Her name is Dana, she posted about a senior React role on LinkedIn. I want to express interest and ask for a call.
evals.expected_output: Should load references/hebrew-style.md BEFORE drafting. Should brain_search for past Hebrew corrections. Output should be: 3 lines max, no em dashes, casual Israeli tone, no formal openers like 'שלום' or closers like 'בברכה'. Should NOT use — anywhere in the Hebrew text.
evals.root_cause_tested: hebrew-style-guide — tests whether skill enforces Hebrew formatting rules before drafting

assertions.name: loads_hebrew_style
assertions.description: Agent reads references/hebrew-style.md OR explicitly references Hebrew style rules before drafting

assertions.name: brain_search_corrections
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search for past Hebrew corrections or user-correction before drafting

assertions.name: no_em_dash
assertions.description: Draft contains no em dash character (—) in the Hebrew text

assertions.name: three_lines_max
assertions.description: Hebrew draft is 3 lines or fewer

assertions.name: casual_tone
assertions.description: Uses casual Hebrew (היי, ספר/ספרי, informal forms) not formal/corporate language

evals.name: correction-learning-loop
evals.prompt: Draft a LinkedIn outreach message to a CTO at a fintech company. [User responds: 'Too long, this isn't corporate America. Make it 2 lines, no sign-off.' Coach redrafts.] Now: next time I ask for outreach to a CTO, what will you do differently?
evals.expected_output: Should brain_store the correction immediately after the user feedback (what was wrong, what they wanted). When asked what it will do differently, should explain it stored the correction and will brain_search for 'user-correction outreach' before drafting next time. The correction should survive as a durable preference.
evals.root_cause_tested: correction-learning-loop — tests whether corrections are stored and surfaced proactively

assertions.name: brain_store_on_correction
assertions.description: After user says 'too long/not like that', agent calls brain_store with the correction tagged 'user-correction'

assertions.name: correction_tagged_coach
assertions.description: brain_store call includes 'coach' and 'user-correction' in tags

assertions.name: explains_future_search
assertions.description: Agent explicitly says it will brain_search for 'user-correction' before drafting next time (not just 'I'll remember')

assertions.name: applies_correction_immediately
assertions.description: Redrafted message is shorter (2 lines or fewer) and matches the corrected preference

evals.name: voice-mode-persistence
evals.prompt: Use voice for this session. What's my top priority today based on my job search status?
evals.expected_output: Should switch to voice_speak for the response. Should brain_search for job search context. Should NOT revert to text for follow-up answers. If asked a follow-up question in this session, should use voice_ask. Voice mode is durable until user says 'text mode' or 'stop voice'.
evals.root_cause_tested: voice-preference-enforcement — tests whether skill makes voice mode sticky within a session

assertions.name: switches_to_voice
assertions.description: Agent calls voice_speak or voice_ask tool (not just text output) after user requests voice mode

assertions.name: brain_search_job_context
assertions.description: Agent calls brain_search for job search or priority context before answering

assertions.name: voice_not_reverted
assertions.description: Agent does NOT switch back to text-only responses within the same session without explicit user instruction

assertions.name: voice_questions_as_voice_ask
